subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the transformed equation of 3x²+10xy+3y²=9 when the axes are rotated through an angle π/4.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.58 — SAQ chapter 8 Transformation of Axes, answer 51.2. Printed appearances: TS 19 · AP,TS M-17 (March 2017) · TS J-16 (June 2016). ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this chapter. But the four STEPS are the book's own: p.59 prints a boxed 'SOLUTION STEPS' panel beside answers 52 and 53 giving the method in exactly four moves — (1) take the given equation as the original (or as the new one), (2) write the change-of-axes formulas, (3) put them into the given equation, (4) simplify to get the answer. This answer is cut on those four printed moves at one mark each, so the DECOMPOSITION is sourced even though the per-step marks are not. Four equal marks also matches the only 4-mark shape the sister chapter prints (Locus answers 44 and 46 carry printed tags, and this chapter's answers are the same length). steps.why: The first move is to label which equation you were handed. A transformation question is always one of two shapes — given the original find the new, or given the new find the original — and every later step depends on which.
common_mistakes: Treating the given equation as the new one.
Dropping a coefficient when copying it down.

steps.label: Write the change of axes
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Under a rotation the old coordinates mix BOTH new ones: x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ and y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ. Put θ = π/4 = 45° and read off the values.
steps.memory_tip: Under a rotation each old coordinate mixes BOTH new ones: x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ, y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ.
lines: Angle of rotation θ = π/4 = 45°, then

recall.must_convey: That the rotation formulas x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ, y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ are written with θ = π/4 = 45°.

steps.why: Under a rotation through θ the old coordinates are mixtures of both new ones: x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ and y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ. Writing them down correctly is most of the work.
common_mistakes: Writing x = Xcosθ + Ysinθ — the sign on the sine term is negative for x.
Swapping the two formulas so that y gets the minus sign.

steps.label: Substitute into the equation
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Put both lines into equation (1). Everything sits over a common denominator, so clearing it once at the end keeps the working short.
steps.memory_tip: Everything sits over the same denominator 2 — clear it once at the end.

steps.why: Substitution is mechanical once the formulas are down. Every x and every y in the given equation is replaced, including the ones inside a squared bracket.
common_mistakes: Substituting into the squared terms but not the xy term.
Losing the denominator on one term only.

steps.label: Simplify to the answer
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Expand and collect. The whole point of choosing this angle is that the XY terms cancel — if an XY term survives, an expansion went wrong.
steps.memory_tip: The angle was chosen so the XY terms CANCEL. A surviving XY term means an expansion went wrong.

recall.must_convey: That expanding and collecting cancels the XY terms and leaves 8X² − 2Y² = 9.

steps.why: These angles are chosen precisely so the cross term vanishes — a surviving XY term is the clearest sign that a bracket was expanded wrongly.
common_mistakes: Leaving an XY term in the answer.
Forgetting to clear the common denominator at the end.

insider_note: The original equation is given, so substitute x = (X − Y)/√2 and y = (X + Y)/√2 — the minus sign belongs to x. The XY terms must cancel; if one survives, a sine term carried the wrong sign.
